title: Plasma AI Formally Proves Erdős Problem #111 on Bipartite-Edge Cuts of Uncountably Chromatic Graphs
aiSystem: Plasma AI (GPT-6 Astra + Claude Opus 5.5 + Lean 4)
whyItMatters: Settles the 45-year-old 1981 Erdős–Hajnal–Szemerédi conjecture (Erdős #111) in infinitary graph theory via a public, Comparator-verified Lean 4 proof.
summary: Using GPT-6 Astra in Codex together with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, Plasma AI produced and formally verified a complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős Problem #111, posed by Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi in 1981. The theorem proves that for every graph G that is not countably colorable (and in particular every graph of chromatic number ℵ₁), the function h_G(n)—measuring the maximum number of edges that must be deleted from an n-vertex subgraph to make it bipartite—satisfies h_G(n)/n → ∞ as n → ∞.
technicalHighlights: Resolves Erdős Problem #111 (Erdős–Hajnal–Szemerédi, 1981), open for 45 years.
Proves h_G(n)/n → ∞ for every non-countably-colorable graph, including graphs with chromatic number ℵ₁.
Machine-checked in Lean 4 with Comparator verification and zero sorrys on public GitHub.
caveats: Released directly as a public Lean 4 repository without an accompanying refereed journal article, though the formal proof is independently reproducible in Lean 4.
